title: Positive thinking
hints: Remember the attribute name in `__set_name__` (`self.name = name`). Don't store values on `self`, because the descriptor is shared by every `Product`. Store them on `obj`.

In `__set__`, validate first (`isinstance(value, bool)` must be checked explicitly, since `bool` is a subclass of `int`) and then write `obj.__dict__[self.name] = value`. In `__get__`, return `self` when `obj is None`.

def __get__(self, obj, owner=None):
    if obj is None: return self
    try: value: float = obj.__dict__[self.name]
    except KeyError: raise AttributeError(f"{self.name} has not been set") from None
    return value
